title: Canonical Semantic Result
description:
Stable semantic interpretation of a recipe ingredient line.

Provenance rule: source_spans identifies the lexical material that produced a semantic object. A child semantic object inherits no provenance implicitly from its parent. Objects that are merely identifiers or labels (e.g. ingredient.id, component.term, package.package_term) do not require their own source_spans when their provenance is already represented by the containing semantic object (reference, quantity, package, modifier, unresolved).

Entity vs. vocabulary boundary: an ingredient is a canonical entity identified by an ingredients.id. A component, measurement unit, natural portion, package, preparation, size, state, descriptor, and other lexical concepts are vocabulary terms. They are not canonical entities merely because they participate in a semantic interpretation. Relationships in the knowledge graph may connect vocabulary terms to ingredient entities, but a relationship does not promote the vocabulary term into an entity. The analyzer may use such relationships as evidence when constructing an interpretation.

Semantic interpretation rules: (1) Entity boundary -- only 'ingredient' references canonical ingredient entities; vocabulary terms do not become entities through relationships. (2) Provenance -- every semantic object produced from lexical material carries the source_spans that produced it. (3) Quantity -- a quantity is either scalar or range, never both. (4) Range syntax -- hyphen and 'to' produce the same range semantics; only source_spans differ. (5) Package -- package count and package size are independent quantities. (6) Per-item -- per_item_quantity establishes per-item scope; no additional flag is required. (7) Modifiers -- every modifier identifies both its vocabulary class (modifier_class) and semantic attachment target (applies_to). (8) Alternatives -- lexical alternatives create relations between separate references; they do not create a combined ingredient. (9) Vocabulary relationships -- knowledge-graph relationships provide evidence for interpretation but do not alter entity/vocabulary type. (10) Unresolved material -- material that cannot be semantically resolved remains explicitly represented rather than being discarded.

status.description: resolved: exactly one interpretation and every semantically required component is resolved. ambiguous: multiple viable interpretations remain. unresolved: interpretation exists, but required semantic material could not be resolved. invalid: no semantically valid interpretation can be produced.

selected_interpretation.description: ID of the selected interpretation. Null when ambiguity remains and no interpretation has been chosen; a single-interpretation result should still populate this once selection policy resolves it.

score.description: Analyzer support score, not a calibrated probability.

unit_term.description: Vocabulary term identifying the measurement or natural-portion unit (e.g. 'cup', 'clove'). Not a canonical entity ID.

count.description: Number of packages (e.g. 2 in '2 cans'). This counts packages, not a measurement or natural-portion quantity, so it is a plain number rather than a Quantity.

package_term.description: Vocabulary term identifying the package/container (e.g. 'can'). Not a canonical entity ID.

size.description: Quantity describing the contents of a single package (e.g. 14 ounce).

modifier_class.description: Vocabulary dimension of the modifier (e.g. 'size', 'state', 'preparation'). Distinct from applies_to: modifier_class describes what kind of modifier this is, applies_to describes what semantic target it attaches to. E.g. modifier_class='preparation', applies_to='ingredient' means 'diced' is a preparation modifier applied to the ingredient; modifier_class='size', applies_to='preparation' means 'large' is a size modifier applied to the preparation (as in 'large dice').

source_spans.description: Lexical provenance for the connective that produced this relation, e.g. the span(s) covering 'and'/'or'.

record_id.description: Identifies a persisted knowledge record appropriate to 'kind'. No universal foreign-key semantics are encoded here; interpretation of record_id is scoped by kind (e.g. kind='relationship_match' -> a relationship row ID; kind='alias_match' -> an ingredient alias record ID).
